data.title: Pitted keratolysis — viva
data.summary: Bacterial infections · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pitted keratolysis** (Bacterial infections)_

**Q1. What is pitted keratolysis?**
- Non-inflammatory superficial infection of the thick stratum corneum of the soles (occasionally palms) producing small crateriform pits; usually asymptomatic but malodorous

**Q2. Causative organisms?**
- Kytococcus sedentarius (formerly Micrococcus), Corynebacterium species, Dermatophilus congolensis, Actinomyces
- They produce keratin-degrading proteases (keratinases) and sulphur compounds (thiols, thioesters) that cause the smell

**Q3. Predisposing factors?**
- Hyperhidrosis, occlusive footwear (soldiers, athletes, farmers in wet fields, policemen, sailors)
- Hot humid climate, prolonged water immersion

**Q4. Describe the clinical features.**
- Multiple 1–7 mm punched-out pits on the weight-bearing areas (heels, balls of the feet, toes); may coalesce into crateriform / shallow erosions
- More prominent when the sole is wet (white macerated look)
- Malodour (bromhidrosis), hyperhidrosis, sliminess, sometimes soreness or itching (painful plaque-like variant)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis?**
- Tinea pedis (scaling, KOH positive), plantar warts (pinpoint black dots, interrupted dermatoglyphics), punctate palmoplantar keratoderma, basal cell naevus syndrome pits (palms), arsenical keratoses, erythrasma of toe webs, juvenile plantar dermatosis

**Q6. Investigations?**
- Clinical; Wood's lamp may show coral-red fluorescence (corynebacteria)
- Gram stain of shaved keratin shows Gram-positive filaments and cocci; culture rarely needed
- Histology: crater in stratum corneum with organisms at the base (seen with PAS/Gram stain)

**Q7. Treatment?**
- Topical antibiotics: erythromycin, clindamycin, fusidic acid, mupirocin; benzoyl peroxide (also deodorises); azole creams (imidazoles act on Gram-positives too)
- Control sweating: aluminium chloride hexahydrate 20%, iontophoresis, botulinum toxin; absorbent cotton socks changed daily, open/breathable footwear, avoid prolonged occlusion
- Oral erythromycin in extensive or resistant cases

**Q8. Why does pitted keratolysis smell?**
- Bacterial breakdown products — sulphur-containing thiols, thioesters and sulphides

**Q9. Dermoscopy of pitted keratolysis.**
- Multiple well-demarcated crateriform depressions with visible walls; organisms seen as filaments in the pit walls on high magnification (Gram stain of shaving)

**Q10. Why might pitted keratolysis be painful?**
- Rare painful plaque-like variant — deep pits in thick plantar skin with soreness on weight bearing, especially in soldiers/athletes; responds to topical antibiotics plus hyperhidrosis control

## Quick spotter facts
- Pits on soles + foul smell + sweaty feet — pitted keratolysis
- Organism: Kytococcus sedentarius

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (ch. Pyodermas); Rook's Textbook of Dermatology for cross-check. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
